pr_title: kv: replace SystemSpanConfig with SystemDescriptorTableSpan / SystemZonesTableSpan
pr_body:
SystemSpanConfig does not have to contain all tables with id <= 10.
It has been replaced with SystemDescriptorTableSpan and SystemZonesTableSpan.
These two tables are the only system tables that are unsplittable.

We cannot get rid of the concept entirely due to SystemSpanConfig components
being relied on for replication reports and opt catalog.

Release note: None

fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/82178
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/82281)

> Honestly, that package existed to compare the span configs infra against the old thing, the old thing we've now gotten rid of. I'd be happy nuking that entire test package. Wanna do the honours?

I'm not convinced we're ready for that. Recall that the optimizer and the replication reports still derive their expectations of what the span configs will be from the pre-existing logic.
Also anyone have an idea on why `TestStoreRangeUpReplicate` and `TestRangeCount` pass locally for me but not in CI?

>For example, is the thrust of this change also going to cause kvserver/reports/reporter.go to use the new descriptor/zones?

No, that's out of scope for this change. This change is to make it such that the system config span tables can be split and such that the trigger concepts are removed. There are still several components which interact with the `config.SystemConfig` object, but get it through a rangefeed. This is safe for secondary tenants to use for the existing use cases they are needed for, so there's nothing pressing us to change it; the span config infrastructure derives its state from the data in descriptor and zones, so nothing about their logic needs to change. 

The two primary users of the SystemConfigProvider are the optimizer and the replication reports.

> spanconfigcompared 

Also I deleted this package, I updated some of the range tests, the one thats kind of suspect to me is `TestStoreRangeUpReplicate` in `client_raft_test.go`

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/90054c6b7b9629aeb904ffd4c0b9161f70e214b7/pkg/sql/catalog/bootstrap/metadata.go#L184-L186

Should we get rid of this condition? It's the reason for the bazel flake, and, I suspect, the need for one of your succeeds soon

Alright I think I addressed everything, thanks for the reviews!

bors r+

issue_context.title: keys,*: eliminate the concept of a `SystemConfigSpan`
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Now that https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/70560 is over and shipped, we can make the system config span a normal key span and rid our codebase of the concept. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd start by deleting the symbols and seeing what happens. We'll want to change the span config logic which currently deals with it.

**Additional context**

This is in the way of https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/81457 because that change wants to add a secondary index to `system.users` and the index code wants to split off the index. We could definitely just work around that, but it feels good to have a push. 

Jira issue: CRDB-16240

review_comments: Perhaps reword some of this commentary to explain why for the system tenant we're choosing to split at SystemConfigSplitKey. I'll actually suggest using TableDataMin here instead (removing another occurrence of "SystemConfig" from SystemConfigSplitKey).

Do we need this anymore? We don't need to be gossiping writes to these two tables, right? IIUC, it was only there for compatibility with 21.2 versions, which this code (to-be-released in v22.2) doesn't care about.

You marked this as resolved, here I meant to ask specifically if we care about gossipping writes to these two sub-spans anymore (`keys.System{Descriptor,Zones}TableSpan`). I don't think we do, so they can be removed.
